GraceChangeDesignContext.NormativeStatus: non-normative; spec.xml wins on every conflict
GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
The accepted M1.3 architecture intentionally separates browser product services from the engine provider. The previous bounded slice proved this model with tabs and durable history; this slice applies the same pattern to two higher-risk domains containing filesystem-adjacent state and secrets.
The current low-level cookie primitive intentionally exposes complete Cookie objects, including raw values. That is appropriate only behind a narrower product boundary. The service therefore separates metadata and value authority rather than publishing the engine DTO unchanged.
The current low-level download surfaces contain destination-path text. Product-level download semantics must not promote those strings into filesystem authority. Completed content should become an opaque generic artifact/blob capability, while the downloads service owns durable metadata and lifecycle state.
Download side effects also differ from tabs/history because start/cancel outcomes may cross a process or I/O boundary before the service receives a definitive result. The service therefore follows M0.7 incomplete-outcome semantics and reconciles rather than blindly retrying.
Chromium remains the source of truth for cookie values and engine-managed storage. Worldline service state stores only product policy, durable download records and projections required for recovery.

Alternatives.Alternative: Expose engine.cookies/0.1 directly to UI and agents. Rejected because metadata-only consumers would necessarily receive cookie secrets and product policy would be coupled to the engine primitive.
Persist a second Worldline cookie database. Rejected because two authoritative cookie stores would create divergence across Chromium/network mutations, expiration and restart.
Store completed download destination_path as the user-visible artifact. Rejected because a path is host implementation detail and possession of a string must not become filesystem authority.
Automatically retry a download start after timeout or provider crash. Rejected because the first start may already have produced an external side effect.

Implement third-party cookie blocking in this bundle. Rejected because network-time request/cookie interception belongs with the later request-policy provider seam and has different callback/deadline semantics.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Final save/export to arbitrary user filesystem locations is deferred until Worldline has an explicit generic authorized sink/filesystem capability or equivalent host boundary.
Network-time third-party cookie restrictions and request interception are deferred to C-BROWSER-REQUEST-POLICY-ADBLOCK-20260901.
Malware/reputation inspection of downloaded artifacts is deferred to a future replaceable service rather than embedded in downloads core.
Final downloads and cookies settings UI belongs to M1.4 composition.
Stable v1 promotion of downloads/cookies/site-data service contracts is deferred until real UI/agent consumers provide compatibility evidence.

Scenarios.Scenario: A caller with admitted page/download authority asks browser.downloads/0.1 to start a deterministic loopback download. The service first creates its durable DownloadRecordId, invokes the engine through bounded authority, observes completion, converts completed content to an opaque artifact reference and persists only product metadata plus that reference. A reader without artifact-read authority can inspect status but cannot read bytes.

The engine accepts a download but the service loses the RPC result before commit is known. After restart the record is Incomplete/Reconciling. Reconciliation finds the existing engine operation or completion fact and updates the same record; no second download is started automatically.

Two persistent contexts visit the same loopback origin and hold different cookie values. A metadata-only principal sees permitted cookie metadata but no value. A separately authorized principal reads the value from Context A but cannot read Context B. Restarting the cookies service does not duplicate cookie state because Chromium remains authoritative.
Both contexts contain localStorage for the same origin. An authorized browser.site-data clear against Context A removes only A's requested storage class; Context B remains unchanged.

Downloads or cookies service is terminated while tabs/history and the real engine provider remain active. Ordinary browsing continues. The terminated service later reconstructs only its own durable state and engine projection.
